newsitem.title: USA: Stocks set first record in New Year, gold tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Stocks set first record in New Year, gold tumbles.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average set its first record of 1997 Monday while the price of gold fell to its lowest level in more than three years.
Oil prices rose. Bonds and the dollar fell.

The Dow Jones industrials rose 23.09 points to 6,567.18, building on its 44 record finishes in 1996, the last one at 6,560.91 on Dec. 27. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,396 to 1,110 on active volume of 527 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, weighted with high-technology issues, also set a record, rising 5.72 points to 1,316.40.
Despite the records for those indexes, Wall Street's overall performance was mixed, with broad indicators exhibiting little of the momentum showed by blue-chip and high-technology issues.
Even the 30-stock Dow index, which raced up nearly 75 points in early trading, ended well off its peak, pulled down by a series of computer selling programmes in late trading.
The strength in stocks was concentrated among economically sensitive companies, which benefited from a growing perception that the economy was still expanding at a solid pace.

"There's no question that the recent numbers have continued to run on the strong side," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "Housing, construction and consumer confidence have all been strong. The first implication of all that is just better (corporate) earnings."
The earnings argument that propelled the Dow to a 101.60-point gain on Friday held sway for most of the session, traders and analysts said, fuelling Monday's rally.
But even as stocks were rising, fear that economic growth could also bring higher inflation ate away at the bond market, where interest rates crept steadily higher all day.
The bellwether 30-year Treasury fell half a point, or $5 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.77 percent from 6.73 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

"If rates are trending higher, you don't buy bank stocks and bank stocks were weak today," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "That shows the thought of higher rates was creeping into investment decisions."
Meanwhile, investors gave gold the cold shoulder in favour of stocks, prompting some analysts to predict the precious metal may be in for an even bigger drop.

The active February gold contract fell $3.30 to $358.70 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange after tumbling $4.60 on Friday. The last time gold traded at current levels was in early October 1993, when it hovered at $350.00.
In currency markets, the dollar lost ground after a Japanese official warned his country would not tolerate "excessive" moves in the foreign exchange markets.
The dollar fell to 115.72 Japanese yen late in New York from 116.33 late on Friday. It fell to 1.5637 German marks from 1.5660 late on Friday.
February crude oil soared 78 cents to $26.37 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange, nearing its six-year high of $26.80 set in late December.
Overseas, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 average rose 84.65 points to 19,446.00 and London's FTSE 100 index added 17 points to 4,106.5.
